Main.sentence: The South Side is one of the three major sections of the city of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , Illinois, United States.

Geographically, it is the largest of the sections of the city, with the other two being the ___E:North U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Side,_Chicago)___ and ___E:West Sides U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side,_Chicago)___ .
It radiates from and lies south of the city's downtown area, the ___E:Chicago Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop)___ .
Much of the South Side came from the city's annexation of townships such as ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park_Township,_Cook_County,_Illinois)___ .
The city's Sides have historically been divided by the ___E:Chicago River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_River)___ and its branches.

The South Side of Chicago was originally defined as all of the city south of the main branch of the Chicago River,   but it now excludes the Loop.  The South Side has a varied ethnic composition and a great variety of income levels and other ___E:demographic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic)___ measures.

It has a reputation for crime, although most crime is contained within certain neighborhoods, not throughout the South Side itself,   and residents range from affluent to middle class to poor.   South Side neighborhoods such as ___E:Armour Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armour_Square,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Back of the Yards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_City,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Bridgeport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ host more ___E:blue collar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_collar)___ and ___E:middle-class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-class)___ residents, while ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ , the ___E:Jackson Park Highlands District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Park_Highlands_District)___ , ___E:Kenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenwood,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Beverly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Mount Greenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Greenwood,_Chicago)___ , and west ___E:Morgan Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Park,_Chicago)___ range from middle class to more affluent residents.
The South Side features professional sports teams, landmark buildings, museums, educational institutions, medical institutions, beaches, and major parts of Chicago's parks system.

The South Side has numerous bus routes and ___E:'L' U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_%27L%27)___ train lines via the ___E:Chicago Transit Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Transit_Authority)___ , it hosts ___E:Midway International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_International_Airport)___ , and includes several ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra)___ rail commuter lines.

There are portions of the U.S. ___E:Interstate Highway System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_Highway_System)___ and also ___E:national highways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Numbered_Highways)___ such as ___E:Lake Shore Drive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Shore_Drive)___ .
There is some debate as to the South Side's boundaries.
Originally the sides were taken from the banks of the Chicago River.

The city's ___E:address numbering system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streets_and_highways_of_Chicago)___ uses a grid demarcating ___E:Madison Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Street_(Chicago))___ as the east–west axis and ___E:State Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Street_(Chicago))___ as the north–south axis. Madison is in the middle of the Loop.  As a result, much of the downtown "Loop" district is south of Madison Street, and the river, but the Loop is usually excluded from any of the Sides.

One definition has the South Side beginning at ___E:Roosevelt Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Road)___ , at the Loop's southern boundary, with the ___E:community area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_in_Chicago)___ known as the ___E:Near South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near_South_Side,_Chicago)___ immediately adjacent.

Another definition, taking into account that much of the Near South Side is in effect part of the commercial district extending in an unbroken line from the South Loop, locates the boundary immediately south of 18th Street or ___E:Cermak Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cermak_Road)___ , where Chinatown in the Armour Square community area begins.
___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ and the ___E:Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana)___ state line provide eastern boundaries.
The southern border changed over time because of Chicago's evolving city limits.
The city limits are now at 138th Street, in ___E:Riverdale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Chicago)___ and ___E:Hegewisch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hegewisch,_Chicago)___ .
The South Side is larger in area than the North and West Sides combined.

Out of 77 community areas in the city, the South Side of Chicago comprises a total of 42 neighborhoods, with some divided into different regions of the area or consolidated into Chicago as part of the annexation of various townships within ___E:Cook County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois)___ .
The exact boundaries dividing the Southwest, South, and Southeast Sides vary by source.

If primarily ___E:racial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation)___ lines are followed, the South Side can generally be divided into a White and Hispanic Southwest Side, a largely Black South Side and a smaller, more racially diverse Southeast Side centered on the ___E:East Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Side,_Chicago)___ community area and including the adjacent community areas of ___E:South Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Chicago,_Chicago)___ , ___E:South Deering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Deering,_Chicago)___ and ___E:Hegewisch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hegewisch,_Chicago)___ .
The differing interpretations of the boundary between the South and Southwest Sides are due to a lack of a definite natural or artificial boundary.
One source states that the boundary is ___E:Western Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Avenue_(Chicago))___ or the railroad tracks adjacent to Western Avenue.
This border extends further south to a former railroad right of way paralleling Beverly Avenue and then ___E:Interstate 57 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_57)___ .
The Southwest Side of Chicago is a subsection of the South Side comprising mainly white, black, and Hispanic neighborhoods, usually dominated by one of these races.

On the Southwest Side exclusively, the northern portion has a high concentration of Hispanics, the western portion has a high concentration of whites, and the eastern portion has a high concentration of blacks.
Architecturally, the Southwest Side is distinguished by the tract of Chicago's Bungalow Belt, which runs through it.

___E:Archer Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archer_Heights)___ , a ___E:Polish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American)___ enclave along ___E:Archer Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archer_Avenue,_Chicago)___ , which leads toward ___E:Midway Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Midway_International_Airport)___ , is located on the Southwest Side of the city, as are ___E:Beverly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly,_Chicago)___ and ___E:Morgan Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Park,_Chicago)___ , home to a large concentration of ___E:Irish Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_American)___ .

With its factories, steel mills and ___E:meat-packing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat_packing_industry)___ plants, the South Side saw a sustained period of immigration which began around the 1840s and continued through ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ . ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people)___ , ___E:Italian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_people)___ , ___E:Polish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_people)___ , ___E:Lithuanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanians)___ and ___E:Yugoslav U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavs)___ immigrants, in particular, settled in neighborhoods adjacent to industrial zones.

The ___E:Illinois Constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Constitution)___ gave rise to townships that provided municipal services in 1850. Several settlements surrounding Chicago incorporated as townships to better serve their residents.
Growth and prosperity overburdened many local government systems.
In 1889, most of these townships determined that they would be better off as part of a larger city of Chicago.

Lake View, Jefferson, Lake, Hyde Park Townships and the Austin portion of ___E:Cicero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero,_Illinois)___ voted to be annexed by the city in the June 29, 1889, elections.

After the ___E:Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ freed millions of slaves, during ___E:Reconstruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era_of_the_United_States)___ black southerners migrated to Chicago and caused the black population to nearly quadruple from 4,000 to 15,000 between 1870 and 1890.

In the 20th century, the numbers expanded with the ___E:Great Migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ , as blacks left the agrarian South seeking a better future in the industrial North, including the South Side. By 1910, the black population in Chicago reached 40,000, with 78% residing in the Black Belt.   Extending 30 blocks, mostly between 31st and 55th Streets,  along ___E:State Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Street_(Chicago))___ , but only a few blocks wide,  it developed into a vibrant community dominated by black businesses, music, food and culture.

As more blacks moved into the South Side, descendants of earlier immigrants, such as ethnic Irish, began to move out. Later housing pressures and civic unrest caused more whites to leave the area and the city. Older residents of means moved to newer ___E:suburban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburb)___ housing as new migrants entered the city,   driving further demographic changes.
The South Side was ___E:racially segregated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation)___ for many decades.

During the 1920s and 1930s, housing cases on the South Side such as Hansberry v. Lee , ___E:311 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Supreme_Court_cases,_volume_311)___ ___E:U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Reports)___ ___E:32 U:(https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/311/32/)___ (1940), went to the ___E:U. S. Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ .

The case, which reset the limitations of ___E:res judicata U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Res_judicata)___ , successfully challenged racial restrictions in the ___E:Washington Park Subdivision U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_Subdivision)___ by reopening them for legal argument.
Blacks resided in ___E:Bronzeville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronzeville,_Chicago)___ (around 35th and State Streets) in an area called "the Black Belt".
After ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , blacks spread across the South Side; its center, east, and western portions.
The Black Belt arose from discriminatory real estate practices by whites against blacks and other racial groups.

In the early 1960s,  during the tenure of then Mayor ___E:Richard J. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley)___ , the construction of the ___E:Dan Ryan Expressway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Ryan_Expressway)___ created controversy.

Many perceived the highway's location as an intentional physical barrier between white and black neighborhoods,  particularly as the Dan Ryan divided Daley's own neighborhood, the traditionally Irish Bridgeport, from Bronzeville.
The economic conditions that led to migration into the South Side were not sustained.

Mid-century industrial restructuring in meat packing and the steel industry cost many jobs. Blacks who became educated and achieved middle-class jobs also left after the ___E:Civil Rights Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Movement)___ to other parts of the city.

Street gangs have been prominent in some South Side neighborhoods for over a century, beginning with those of Irish immigrants, who established the first territories in a struggle against other European and black migrants.

Some other neighborhoods stayed relatively safe for a big city. By the 1960s, gangs such as the ___E:Vice Lords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Lords)___ began to improve their public image, shifting from criminal ventures to operating social programs funded by government and private grants.
However, in the 1970s gangs returned to violence and the drug trade.
By 2000, traditionally all-male gangs crossed gender lines to include about 20% females.
By the 1930s, the city of Chicago boasted that over 25% of its residential structures were less than 10 years old, many of which were ___E:bungalows U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungalow)___ .

These continued to be built in the working-class South Side into the 1960s.   ___E:Studio apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_apartment)___ , with ___E:Murphy beds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murphy_bed)___ and ___E:kitchenettes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchenettes)___ or ___E:Pullman kitchens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pullman_kitchen&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , comprised a large part of the housing supply during and after the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , especially in the "Black Belt".
The South Side had a history of ___E:philanthropic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philanthropist)___ subsidized housing dating back to 1919.

The ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ passed the ___E:Housing Act of 1949 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_Act_of_1949)___ to fund and improve public housing.

CHA produced a plan of citywide projects, which was rejected by the ___E:Chicago City Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_City_Council)___ 's white aldermen who opposed public housing in their wards.
This led to a CHA policy of construction of family housing only in black residential areas, concentrated on the South and West Sides.
Historian ___E:Arnold R. Hirsch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_R._Hirsch)___ said the CHA was "a bulwark of segregation that helped sustain Chicago's 'second ghetto'".

Gentrification of parts of the ___E:Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas,_Chicago)___ community area has bolstered the ___E:Black Metropolis-Bronzeville District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Metropolis-Bronzeville_District)___ .
Gentrification in various parts of the South Side has displaced many black citizens.
The South Side offers numerous housing ___E:cooperatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative)___ .

Hyde Park has several ___E:middle-income U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-income)___ co-ops and other South Side regions have limited equity (subsidized, price-controlled) co-ops.  These regions experienced ___E:condominium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condominium_(living_space))___ construction and conversion in the 1970s and 1980s.

In the late 20th century, the South Side had some of the poorest housing conditions in the U.S., but the ___E:Chicago Housing Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Housing_Authority)___ (CHA) began replacing the old high-rise public housing with ___E:mixed-income U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed-income_housing)___ , lower-density developments, part of the city's Plan for Transformation.
Many of the CHA's massive public housing projects, which lined several miles of South State Street, have been demolished.
Among the largest were the ___E:Robert Taylor Homes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Taylor_Homes)___ .

Some ___E:census tracts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_tract)___ (4904 in ___E:Roseland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseland,_Chicago)___ , 7106 in ___E:Auburn Gresham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Gresham,_Chicago)___ ) are 99% black.

Hyde Park is home to the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ , as well as the South Side's largest ___E:Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jew)___ population, centered on Chicago's oldest ___E:synagogue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synagogue)___ , the ___E:Chicago Landmark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Landmark)___ ___E:KAM Isaiah Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KAM_Isaiah_Israel)___ .

The Southwest Side's ethnic makeup also includes the largest concentration of ___E:Gorals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorals)___ ( ___E:Carpathian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpathian_mountains)___ highlanders) outside of Europe; it is the location of the ___E:Polish Highlanders Alliance of North America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Highlanders_Alliance_of_North_America)___ .
A large ___E:Mexican-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican-American)___ population resides in Little Village (South Lawndale) and areas south of 99th Street.

The ___E:South Side Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side_Irish)___ Parade occurs in the ___E:Beverly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly,_Chicago)___ neighborhood along ___E:Western Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Avenue_(Chicago))___ each year on the Sunday before ___E:St. Patrick's Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick%27s_Day)___ .

The parade, which was founded in 1979, was at one time said to be the largest Irish neighborhood St. Patrick's celebration in the world outside of ___E:Dublin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin)___ , ___E:Ireland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland)___ ,  and was—until being scaled back in 2012—actually larger than Chicago's other St. Patrick's Day parade in the Loop. The South Side parade became such an event that it was broadcast on Chicago's ___E:CBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS)___ ___E:affiliate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affiliate_network)___ .
Following the 2009 parade, organizers stated the group was "not planning to stage a parade in its present form".
The parade was cancelled in 2010 and 2011 before being revived with more strict security and law enforcement.

The ___E:Bud Billiken Parade and Picnic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Billiken_Parade_and_Picnic)___ , the second largest parade in the U.S. and the nation's largest black parade,  runs annually on Martin Luther King Drive between 31st and 51st Streets in the Bronzeville neighborhood, through the main portion of the South Side.

Neighborhood rehabilitation, and in some cases, gentrification, can be seen in parts of ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park,_Chicago_(Community_area))___ , ___E:Woodlawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodlawn,_Chicago)___ (#42) and Bronzeville, as well as in Bridgeport and McKinley Park. Historic ___E:Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ 's redevelopment is another example of a work in progress. ___E:Chinatown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown,_Chicago)___ is located on the South Side and has seen a surge in growth.

It has become an increasingly popular destination for both tourists and locals alike and is a cornerstone of the city's ___E:Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Chinese)___ community. [citation needed] The South Side offers many outdoor amenities, such as miles of public lakefront parks and beaches, as it borders Lake Michigan on its eastern side. [citation needed]
Today's South Side is mostly a combination of the former Hyde Park and Lake Townships.
Within these townships many had made speculative bets on future prosperity.

Much of the South Side evolved from these speculative investments. ___E:Stephen A. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_A._Douglas)___ , ___E:Paul Cornell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Cornell_(lawyer))___ , ___E:George Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Pullman)___ and various business entities developed South Chicago real estate.

The ___E:Pullman District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ , a former company town, Hyde Park Township, various platted communities and subdivisions were the results of such efforts.

The ___E:Union Stock Yards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Stock_Yards)___ , which were once located in the ___E:New City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_City,_Chicago)___ community area (#61), at one point employed 25,000 people and produced 82 percent of US domestic meat production.

They were so synonymous with the city that for over a century they were part of the lyrics of ___E:Frank Sinatra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra)___ 's " ___E:My Kind of Town U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Kind_of_Town)___ ", in the phrase: "The Union Stock Yard, Chicago is ..." The ___E:Union Stock Yard Gate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Stock_Yard_Gate)___ marking the old entrance to stockyards was designated a Chicago Landmark on February 24, 1972,  and a ___E:National Historic Landmark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark)___ on May 29, 1981.

Other South Side regions have been known for great wealth, such as ___E:Prairie Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie_Avenue)___ . 21st century redevelopment includes ___E:One Museum Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Museum_Park)___ and ___E:One Museum Park West U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Museum_Park_West)___ .
The South Side accommodates much of the city's conference business with various ___E:convention centers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_center)___ .
The current ___E:McCormick Place U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCormick_Place)___ Convention Center is the largest convention center in the U.S. and the third largest in the world.

Previously, the South Side hosted conventions at the ___E:Chicago Coliseum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Coliseum)___ and the ___E:International Amphitheatre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Amphitheatre)___ .

The ___E:Ford City Mall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_City_Mall)___ and the surrounding shopping district includes several ___E:big-box retailers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big-box_store)___ .
The South Side has been home to some of the most significant figures in the history of American politics.

These include ___E:Richard J. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley)___ and his son, ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ ; the first black ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and former first lady ___E:Michelle Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ ; the first black female ___E:U.S. Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senator)___ , ___E:Carol Moseley Braun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Moseley_Braun)___ ; and the first black presidential candidate to win a primary, ___E:Jesse Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Jackson)___ .

Before them, ___E:Harold Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington)___ , a ___E:Congressman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and the first black ___E:Mayor of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ , as well as groundbreaking Congressman ___E:William L. Dawson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_L._Dawson_(politician))___ , achieved political success from the South Side.

The ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ is one of the world's leading universities, counting 101 affiliated ___E:Nobel laureates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_laureates)___ .

At ___E:Chicago Pile-1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Pile-1)___ at the university, the first self-sustaining ___E:nuclear chain reaction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_chain_reaction)___ was achieved under the direction of ___E:Enrico Fermi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrico_Fermi)___ in the 1940s.

Other four-year educational institutions there are the ___E:Illinois Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Institute_of_Technology)___ , ___E:St. Xavier University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier_University)___ , ___E:Chicago State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_State_University)___ , ___E:Illinois College of Optometry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_College_of_Optometry)___ and ___E:Shimer College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimer_College)___ .

The South Side also hosts ___E:community colleges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_college)___ such as ___E:Olive-Harvey College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive-Harvey_College)___ , ___E:Kennedy-King College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy-King_College)___ and ___E:Richard J. Daley College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley_College)___ .

___E:Chicago Public Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Public_Schools)___ operates the public schools on the South Side, including ___E:DuSable High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuSable_High_School)___ , ___E:Simeon Career Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simeon_Career_Academy)___ , ___E:John Hope College Prep High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hope_College_Prep_High_School)___ and ___E:Phillips Academy High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_Academy_High_School)___ .

The ___E:De La Salle Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_La_Salle_Institute)___ , located in the ___E:Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas,_Chicago)___ community area across the street from ___E:Chicago Police Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Police_Department)___ headquarters, has taught five ___E:Chicago Mayors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Mayor)___ :  ___E:Richard J. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley)___ , ___E:Michael A. Bilandic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_A._Bilandic)___ , ___E:Martin H. Kennelly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_H._Kennelly)___ , ___E:Frank J. Corr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_J._Corr)___ and ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ .
Three of these mayors hail from the South Side's ___E:Bridgeport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport,_Chicago)___ community area, which also produced two other Chicago Mayors.
___E:University of Chicago Lab School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Lab_School)___ , affiliated with the University of Chicago, is a private school located there.
The South Side is home to many official landmarks and other notable buildings and structures.

It hosts three of the four ___E:Chicago Registered Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Registered_Historic_Places_in_Chicago)___ from the original October 15, 1966 ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ list ( ___E:Chicago Pile-1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Pile-1)___ , ___E:Robie House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robie_House)___ and ___E:Lorado Taft Midway Studios U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorado_Taft_Midway_Studios)___ ).

Chicago's African American community, concentrated on the South Side, experienced an artistic movement from the 1930s until the 1960s.

The movement was concentrated in and around the ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ community area. Prominent writers and artists included ___E:Gwendolyn Brooks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwendolyn_Brooks)___ , ___E:Margaret Burroughs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Burroughs)___ , ___E:Elizabeth Catlett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Catlett)___ , ___E:Eldzier Cortor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldzier_Cortor)___ , ___E:Richard Hunt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Hunt_(sculptor))___ , ___E:Gordon Parks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Parks)___ , and ___E:Richard Wright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Wright_(author))___ .

Other ___E:Chicago Black Renaissance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Black_Renaissance)___ artists included ___E:Willard Motley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willard_Motley)___ , ___E:William Attaway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Attaway)___ , ___E:Frank Marshall Davis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Marshall_Davis)___ , and ___E:Margaret Walker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Walker)___ . ___E:St. Clair Drake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Clair_Drake)___ and ___E:Horace R. Cayton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace_R._Cayton_Jr.)___ represented the new wave of intellectual expression in literature by depicting the culture of the urban ghetto rather than the culture of blacks in ___E:the South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States)___ in the ___E:monograph U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monograph)___ Black Metropolis .
In 1961, Burroughs founded the ___E:DuSable Museum of African American History U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuSable_Museum_of_African_American_History)___ .

By the late 1960s the South Side had a robost art movement led by ___E:Jim Nutt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Nutt)___ , ___E:Gladys Nilsson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladys_Nilsson)___ , ___E:Karl Wirsum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Wirsum)___ and others, who became known as the ___E:Chicago Imagists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Imagists)___ .

Music in Chicago flourished, with musicians bringing ___E:blues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues)___ and ___E:gospel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music)___ influences up from the South and creating a Chicago sound in blues and ___E:jazz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz)___ that the city is still renowned for. The South Side was known for its R&B acts and the city as a while had successful rock acts. Many major and independent record companies had a presence in Chicago.

In 1948, ___E:Blues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues)___ was introduced by ___E:Aristocrat Records U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristocrat_Records)___ (later ___E:Chess Records U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_Records)___ ). ___E:Muddy Waters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muddy_Waters)___ and ___E:Chess Records U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_Records)___ quickly followed with ___E:Chuck Berry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry)___ , ___E:Bo Diddley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Diddley)___ , ___E:Little Walter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Walter)___ , ___E:Jimmy Rogers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Rogers)___ , and ___E:Howlin' Wolf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howlin%27_Wolf)___ .
